summary: Describes cryptographic algorithms and parameters that supplement the original Russian GOST specifications (GOST 28147-89, GOST R 34.10-94, GOST R 34.10-2001, and GOST R 34.11-94) for use in Internet applications. The document is informational.

plainLanguage.summary: This memo adds operating details for several GOST cryptographic algorithms. It describes how to choose modes and parameters, handle keys, and identify settings in Internet applications.

questions: gost cryptographic parameters for internet use
how does gost key wrap work
what are the gost parameter sets
subtitle: Supplementary modes, key handling, and parameter sets for the GOST cryptographic algorithms.

tldr.problem: The referenced GOST standards provide basic algorithm descriptions but leave supplementary details needed by Internet applications.
tldr.mechanism: The memo specifies a CBC mode, padding choices, key meshing, HMAC and pseudorandom-function use, key derivation and wrapping, diversification, and ASN.1 parameter identifiers.
tldr.outcome: This is a CRYPTO-PRO proposal for supplementary algorithm details. It recommends against using test parameter sets or unlisted parameter sets.

today: RFC 4357 is Informational. The work-unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it, and the text describes it as a proposal rather than an Internet standard.

sections.title: Purpose and Scope
sections.content:
The memo supplements GOST 28147-89, GOST R 34.10-94, GOST R 34.10-2001, and GOST R 34.11-94. It presents additional algorithms and parameters for use with Internet applications, as a proposal from CRYPTO-PRO for the Russian Cryptographic Software Compatibility Agreement community.

It defines supporting terms and helper operations used in later sections. When keys and initialization vectors are converted to or from byte arrays, the memo assumes little-endian byte order.
sections.plainLanguage: The document fills in details that the original GOST algorithm descriptions leave open. It is a supplementary proposal for software that needs to use those algorithms consistently.

sections.title: Cipher Modes, Padding, and Key Changes
sections.content:
The memo adds CBC mode for GOST 28147-89. In CBC, each plaintext block is combined with the preceding ciphertext block before encryption; the initialization vector is used for the first block. The cipher's block size is 8 bytes, so the memo also describes zero, PKCS#5, and random padding for data that does not fill a block.

Key meshing changes a symmetric key after processing data. The CryptoPro method transforms the key and initialization vector every 1024 octets. The memo warns that this method cannot resynchronize during decryption if encrypted data is corrupted, lost, or processed out of order. Null key meshing leaves the key unchanged.
sections.plainLanguage: CBC combines each block with the previous encrypted block. Padding fills a final short block, while key meshing can replace the key as data is processed.

sections.title: Message Authentication and Key Derivation
sections.content:
HMAC_GOSTR3411 applies HMAC to the GOST R 34.11-94 hash function. PRF_GOSTR3411 is a pseudorandom function built on that HMAC and calculated using the P_hash construction described in the referenced TLS specification.

The memo defines two VKO key-derivation algorithms for creating a key-encryption key. One uses GOST R 34.10-94 key pairs and hashes a shared secret; the other uses GOST R 34.10-2001 key pairs and a UKM value. The paired keys must use identical parameters, and the memo specifies cases where these procedures must not be used.
sections.plainLanguage: The memo defines a message-authentication method and a pseudorandom function using the GOST hash. It also describes two ways for key pairs to derive a shared key-encryption key.

sections.title: Key Wrapping and Diversification
sections.content:
The key-wrap procedures encrypt a content-encryption key using a key-encryption key. The wrapped value carries a UKM, the encrypted content key, and a checksum. The unwrap procedures check the expected length and verify the checksum after decryption.

CryptoPro key wrap first diversifies the key-encryption key using the UKM. The memo also defines an algorithm to diversify a secret key using diversification data. Key wrapping and diversification are intended to give applications specified procedures for handling keys; their detailed steps are defined in the RFC.
sections.plainLanguage: Key wrapping encrypts one key with another and includes information that lets the receiver check the result. Diversification creates a changed key from an existing key and additional input.

sections.title: Parameter Sets and Security Guidance
sections.content:
The memo uses ASN.1 object identifiers to name proposed parameter sets for the encryption, digest, and public-key algorithms. The sets specify values such as S-boxes, cipher mode, key meshing, digest initialization values, or public-key parameters. Appendices contain the ASN.1 modules and parameter values.

The security section recommends checking signatures, public keys, and algorithm parameters against the corresponding GOST standards before use. It advises against test sets and parameter sets not described in the memo, and recommends that other parameters be examined by an authorized agency using approved cryptographic analysis methods.
sections.plainLanguage: Named parameter sets let applications refer to a defined collection of algorithm settings. The memo recommends checking keys and parameters and avoiding test settings for normal use.
